claude.rationale: Per the structural summary, the whole company crossed as a single going concern with "the product and process tiers cross[ing] intact," and the proxy documents no carve-out of product lines from the transaction — so product (T4) and its producing processes (T5) moved together, yielding gap_45=0. Likewise, the same closing structure kept the operational processes with the operating going concern; the people tier (T6) was bridged by a one-year continuity-of-benefits commitment and pre-existing severance arrangements, so processes and the organization that runs them transferred together within the surviving corporation, yielding gap_56=0. T1 is coded replace because all seven IDT directors ceased serving and the board was reconstituted with two Parent-designated members plus an amended charter/bylaws, installing new controlling intent. T6 is coded partial due to the friction noted at closing (no new individually negotiated retention agreements, only fixed one-year benefits continuity and pre-existing severance).

grok.rationale: The structural summary and product/process section state that the whole company, including all product lines, crossed as a single going concern with no carve-outs, so T4 and T5 moved together and gap_45 is 0. The same going-concern transfer carried the workforce into the surviving corporation, with only a one-year continuity-of-benefits commitment and pre-existing severance bridging T6; that is continuity of the organization alongside processes, not a processes-without-people mismatch at closing, so gap_56 is 0.

openai.rationale: The slice states that the whole company crossed into Parent's ownership as a single going concern, with no product-line or business-unit carve-outs, and that the product and process tiers crossed intact; therefore no T4-T5 structural gap is documented. By contrast, the processes transferred while the people tier had only a one-year continuity-of-benefits commitment and pre-existing severance protections, with no documented employment arrangements between IDT executives and Parent and complete replacement of the seven-member board by two Parent designees. No transitional-services or operating agreement allocating this people-process mismatch is documented.
